analysis.title: Rates Spark: US inflation likely too hot for comfort
key_insights: ING expects US core CPI at 0.3% MoM, which it says is too hot to support lower rates. Consensus sees headline CPI at 0.3% MoM.
The direct pass-through from oil to rates has weakened compared with a few months ago. Rates were much more sensitive to oil prices then, and the correlation has diminished significantly.
Brent oil near $90 per barrel eases inflation risks but does not remove the upside risks. The focus has rotated to potential second-round effects of higher energy costs.

Flows data from recent weeks already showed increased demand for longer-dated bonds, before the AI jitters started. Concerns about stretched equity prices can feed a relative value play in which a 10yr UST yield of around 5% looks attractive.
ING still warns of upside risks to rates in the near term. Markets keep rotating attention between AI and inflation concerns, which keeps volatility high.

The 0.3% MoM CPI forecast is above the 0.17% monthly pace needed to average out at an annualised 2%, the Fed's target. No annual CPI figure will be published because no data was collected for the yearly comparison during the 2025 government shutdown.

Tuesday calendar: US CPI, Fed speakers Waller, Logan, Schmid and Paulson, the BoE Watchers conference with ECB chief economist Lane, an EU syndicated 5y and 20y tap, Netherlands 10y DSL auction (up to EUR 3bn), UK 29y Gilt auction (GBP 1bn) and a US Treasury sale of new 10y notes (US$42bn).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Benchmark for the Fed's 2% target. A 0.3% print would run above it.

A yield near 5% could look attractive against stretched equity prices and supports inflows into longer-dated bonds.

Second-round effects of higher energy costs on inflation.
Renewed AI-related equity weakness and stretched equity prices, which add volatility.

Flows data showed rising demand for longer-dated bonds in recent weeks, and most global 10yr rates ticked a few bp lower on Monday.

tension_points.bull_case: A 10yr UST yield near 5% looks attractive against stretched equity prices and AI jitters, and flows already show demand for longer-dated bonds.
tension_points.bear_case: A 0.3% MoM core CPI is too hot to support lower rates, and second-round effects of energy costs keep upside risk to rates.
